title: Knots touching twice: the identification on most of the census
claim: Lemma M: from round 1 the cheapest parity growth reads a start only through each knot's set of live neighbours and each live knot's open count (multiplicities enter only through open counts). Theorem 6: hence RING-IDENT's, CHAIN-IDENT's and RELAY-IDENT's identification and dimension theorems hold for knot multigraphs, under (S3) and (S4) read on live knots (dead knots as common neighbours and blocks) and (S6') at least two loose distinctions; a one-loose start closes at round 1. Corollary 7: on the touch census the growth class read off the relayed extended complex equals the measured class on all 12,473 arrangements in the class.
standard_statement: As RING-IDENT's; linear algebra over GF(2) for the implied test.
prior_work: RING-IDENT-20261119-001, CHAIN-IDENT-20261119-001, RELAY-IDENT-20261119-001 (simple knot graphs); CLUSTER-ALL-20261119-001 (the rule on the census, computed).
completion_gate: The machine check on the whole touch census (11,512 of 11,512 in the class agree per round; 727 one-loose starts close); ticket B (D1, 12,473 of 12,473); the referee reviews the proof.

validation.status: written in full; statement checked by the advisor before the freeze; referee pending
validation.independence: machine_check.py classifies every census arrangement on Lemma M data and compares per-round (parents, fresh) multisets with the relayed cover

attained_result: Lemma M, Theorem 6 and the one-loose closure proved; Corollary 7 computed in ticket B.
